v11.72 - x-118: bir çözümleme cevabı, sorulduğu taslağa aittir

The New Mission form debounces its "what would this launch with?" request by
220ms, and the generation that guards the answers was bumped inside the timer —
when the request went out — instead of when the draft changed. So for the whole
window between an edit and its own request, the answer already in flight about
the PREVIOUS draft still passed the `m.seq !== previewSeq` gate: it was
accepted, it painted the new draft's model box, effort box and refusal list with
the old resolution, and the repaint it caused cleared and re-armed the debounce,
pushing the new draft's own request another 220ms further away every time it
happened. U-103's "an older answer may not paint over a newer one" was measured
on a stale token only, never on this window, which is the one a typing hand
actually lives in.

The generation is the DRAFT's now, taken synchronously: `schedulePreview`
fingerprints `draftInput()` on the spot, advances `previewSeq` only when that
fingerprint really changed, and the timer sends the generation it captured. An
answer whose token is behind the draft is dropped before it can paint anything
and before it can touch the clock. A repaint that changed nothing — an arriving
answer, a panel data refresh, any of the twenty other reasons this page renders
— finds a pending request for the same draft and leaves it alone rather than
restarting it.

Measured in test/test_missions_webview.js: request A is put in flight, the goal
is edited, A is answered before B's debounce fires — the DOM does not move, B's
timer handle is never cleared (setTimeout/clearTimeout are wrapped to watch the
handle, since a fake clock cannot show 220ms passing), a panel data refresh in
the middle does not clear it either, B's request then goes out one generation
ahead carrying B's own words, and A landing LAST cannot overwrite B's answer.
All three assertions fail on the previous code.

No visual change: this is the timing of a request, not what the page draws.
